title: Equality and hashing (dictionary key contract)
hook: When two objects compare equal, they must produce the same hash code. Break that rule and your Dictionary lookups silently miss — a bug that shows up only under load in a Redis cache or an in-flight attempt tracker.

blocks.text: **Equality** asks whether two values represent the same data. **Hashing** compresses an object into an integer for fast lookup in collections like `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` and `HashSet<T>`. The contract is strict: if `Equals` returns true, `GetHashCode` must return the same value. Classes default to **reference equality** (same object in memory). Records and structs default to **value equality** (same field values).

entries.plainDefinition: Two variables point at the same object in memory. The default for classes.
entries.example: `ReferenceEquals(a, b)` or default `==` for classes without overload.

entries.plainDefinition: Two objects compare equal because their data matches, even if they are different instances.
entries.example: Two `AuthToken` records with the same claims are value-equal.

entries.plainDefinition: Returns an integer hash used by dictionaries and hash sets to bucket entries. Must be consistent with Equals.
Interface with a typed Equals(T other) method. Avoids boxing when T is a struct used in collections.

blocks.text: Every `Dictionary` and `HashSet` uses `GetHashCode` to pick a bucket, then `Equals` to confirm a match. If you override `Equals` but leave the default reference-based `GetHashCode`, equal objects land in different buckets and lookups return nothing. In a Redis-backed in-flight tracker or a high-concurrency submit path, that means duplicate processing or lost cache entries. Records generate a consistent pair automatically; hand-rolled DTOs often do not.

blocks.title: Never mutate a dictionary key
blocks.body: If a key's fields change after insertion, its hash changes and the entry becomes unreachable — a silent orphan in the dictionary. Use immutable records or readonly structs as keys.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

blocks.title: Dictionary lookup using equality and hashing

items.title: Compute hash of the lookup key
items.body: Dictionary calls `key.GetHashCode()` to find the bucket index.

items.title: Scan the bucket
items.body: All entries in that bucket are compared with `Equals`. Matching hash codes do not guarantee equality — hash collisions happen.

items.title: Confirm with Equals
items.body: If `Equals` returns true, the entry is found. If false, the dictionary reports a miss.

items.title: Contract check
items.body: Equal objects must hash equal. Unequal objects may hash equal (collision) but Equals must return false.

diagram.title: Equals and GetHashCode contract
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  LOOKUP[Dictionary lookup] --> HASH[GetHashCode of key]
  HASH --> BUCKET[Find bucket]
  BUCKET --> EQUALS[Equals against entries]
  EQUALS -->|true| FOUND[Return value]
  EQUALS -->|false| MISS[Key not found]
  CONTRACT[Rule: Equals true implies same hash]

snippet.label: IEquatable cache key in a dictionary
snippet.explanation: Line 1: readonly struct implements `IEquatable<AttemptKey>`. Lines 6–7: typed `Equals` avoids boxing. Line 12: `GetHashCode` uses the same fields as `Equals`. Lines 15–16: two different struct copies find the same slot because equality and hash agree.

snippet.label: Reference equality versus value equality
snippet.explanation: Lines 1–4: two lists with identical contents are not equal — classes use reference equality by default. Lines 6–8: two records with the same values are equal even though they are different heap objects. Records generate both `Equals` and `GetHashCode`.

snippet.label: The broken-equality bug
snippet.explanation: Line 5: `Equals` is overridden for value comparison. Line 6: `GetHashCode` is NOT overridden — it still uses the default reference hash. Lines 11–13: `key1` and `key2` are equal by `Equals` but hash differently, so `ContainsKey` returns false. Always override both together.

blocks.title: Equality across languages
rows: Reference equality by default for classes
Typed Equals avoids boxing for structs

blocks.title: Overriding Equals without GetHashCode
blocks.body: This is the most common equality bug. `Dictionary` and `HashSet` will appear to work in simple tests but fail under real data because equal keys land in different buckets.

blocks.title: Mutable DTO as a HashSet element
blocks.body: A mutable class used in a `HashSet` across a high-concurrency submit path will break when any thread changes a field that affects equality. The entry becomes unreachable. Use immutable records or readonly structs.

interviewTakeaways: Equals and GetHashCode are a pair; collections depend on it.
IEquatable<T> avoids boxing for value types.
Never mutate a dictionary key; records help only if they stay immutable.
commonPitfalls: Overriding Equals on a class but leaving the default reference GetHashCode.
Using a mutable DTO as a HashSet element across a high-concurrency submit path.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript objects compare by reference; there is no IEquatable. Map keys use SameValueZero. C# dictionaries use the type's equality contract.
TypeScript cannot generate Equals/GetHashCode. You write your own or use a library. C# records generate both.
